**Future generations** — what the living owe, and why they care about, people who will live after them — longtermism and existential risk, intergenerational justice, the non-identity problem and person-affecting views, population ethics, discounting of future welfare, and the psychology of concern for the future: legacy motivation, generativity, symbolic immortality and continuity with one's future self (ADR-063).

| [THEORY-1562](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1562.md) v2 | Cottingham reports that the third lecture of Scheffler's Death and the Afterlife holds that a life must be temporally bounded for its goods to have the status of values, so that personal immortality is no remedy, and that among the commentators Frankfurt doubts the concern for humanity's continuation is altruistic and Wolf denies that impending extinction would or should undercut our projects | Cottingham (2014), [LIT-1784](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1784.md), read in [NOTE-1306](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1306.md): a short NDPR review, the record's only report of the book's third lecture and commentaries. | [THEORY-1563](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1563.md) v2 | Thorstad argues that on simple models of existential risk higher risk does not raise, and in most variants lowers, the value of reducing it, so that high risk this century is compatible with astronomical value for mitigation only if risk falls soon and stays very low, and that three arguments offered for such a time of perils, from wisdom, an existential risk Kuznets curve and space settlement, are weak, leaving aside the argument from advanced AI | Thorstad (2023), read in full from the GPI working paper, a penultimate draft ([NOTE-1308](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1308.md)), not compared with the published version. | [THEORY-1566](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1566.md) v2 | Tarsney argues that the chance an intervention's effect is nullified acts as an exponential discount, so that under expectational utilitarianism and deliberately pessimistic inputs existential-risk reduction beats a strong global-health benchmark only if nullifying events are rare, and its robust win rests, on some views, on probabilities of order 10^-18 or less | Tarsney (2023), read in full from the 2022 working paper ([NOTE-1247](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1247.md)), not compared with the Synthese text. | [THEORY-1568](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1568.md) v2 | Meyer argues that a threshold notion of harm lets a weakly person-affecting view state harms to future people despite the non-identity problem, best specified as weakly sufficientarian, and that such a view gives no reason to prefer a flourishing future to none, a gap he fills with concerns that rest on what present and past people value and an obligation owed to them | Meyer's SEP entry, Intergenerational Justice, in its 2026 revision ([NOTE-1304](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1304.md)). | [THEORY-1569](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1569.md) v2 | Gardiner argues that climate change joins a global commons problem to an intergenerational one that institutions and reciprocity cannot solve, because the generations do not coexist, and that these, with our theories' weakness, leave each generation open to moral corruption that hides its exploitation of its temporal position, even from itself | Gardiner (2006), read in full ([NOTE-1252](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1252.md)). | [THEORY-1571](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1571.md) v2 | Ramsey argues that a community that lives for ever and does not discount later enjoyments should save at the rate at which saving times the marginal utility of consumption equals the shortfall of present net enjoyment from Bliss, a rule independent of the interest rate, and he calls discounting later enjoyments ethically indefensible, a product of the weakness of the imagination | Ramsey (1928), read in full from a scan of the published article ([NOTE-1287](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1287.md)). The founding text of optimal-growth theory and the reference for refusing to discount the future for being later. | [THEORY-1574](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1574.md) v2 | Bostrom argues that on aggregative, time-neutral views of value reducing existential risk is a global priority, and that it is undersupplied for lack of motivation as well as understanding, since its benefit is a pan-generational public good whose future beneficiaries cannot pay and moral sentiment is insensitive to scope | Bostrom (2013), read in full from the published version ([NOTE-1321](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1321.md)). The longtermist text that says most about motivation. Maxipok holds "whenever we act out of an impersonal concern for humankind as a whole", and Bostrom grants that "Unrestricted altruism is not so common" (p. 19). The risk estimates are subjective, and the motivational diagnosis is theory, not tested. | Active |
| [THEORY-1575](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1575.md) v2 | Narveson argues that creating a person neither benefits nor harms them, that the existence of people with good lives is normally good and a reason to create them though no one is owed it, and that only harm to actual persons can justify coercion over procreation | Narveson's late restatement of the person-affecting view (2017), after giving up utilitarianism, read in full ([NOTE-1318](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1318.md)) in place of his 1973 paper. | [THEORY-1577](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1577.md) v2 | Scheffler argues that the survival of other people after one's death is a condition of much of what matters to us mattering, and matters to us in its own right, and reads this as our dependence on future people rather than altruism toward them | Scheffler's 2012 Tanner Lectures, [LIT-1779](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1779.md), read in [NOTE-1298](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1298.md) in place of Death and the Afterlife ([LIT-1754](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1754.md)). | [THEORY-1579](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1579.md) v2 | Syropoulos et al. report that felt responsibility to future generations is endorsed by most people in Europe and the US, is nearly unrelated to ideology and demographics and half as tied to conservatism as responsibility for climate, predicts self-reported proenvironmentalism, and was raised a little by each of five brief interventions, most by a letter to a person born today and least by a longtermist text | Syropoulos et al., thirteen studies and a preregistered experiment (N = 3,175), read in full from the OSF preprint of 2023 without supplements ([NOTE-1293](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1293.md)), in place of Syropoulos and Markowitz 2021; not compared with the published version. | [THEORY-1604](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1604.md) v2 | Greaves and MacAskill argue that in the most important decisions facing agents today every near-best option is near-best for the far future and delivers much larger benefits there than in the near future, on expected-value reasoning that they concede needs a zero pure rate of time preference and may fail through fanaticism | Greaves and MacAskill, read in full from the 2021 working paper ([NOTE-1302](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1302.md)), not compared with the 2025 chapter the LIT files. | [THEORY-1610](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1610.md) v2 | Parfit argues that narrow person-affecting principles fail in non-identity and different-number cases, and that a wide person-affecting principle, on which being caused to exist with a life worth living is an intrinsic benefit and an outcome is in one way worse if it benefits people less, solves the non-identity problem and keeps the relation of being better transitive | Parfit's last paper (2017), read in full and unfinished by the editor's note ([NOTE-1263](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1263.md)). | [THEORY-1633](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1633.md) v2 | Bostrom argues that delay in settling the local supercluster loses potential lives at a vast rate, but that on a total, undiscounted view even a small cut in existential risk outweighs any feasible acceleration, while on a person-affecting view, given some chance that people now alive share the cosmic future, safety must be balanced against speed | Bostrom's Astronomical Waste (2003), read in full from the author's HTML ([NOTE-1314](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1314.md)), not compared with the journal text. | [THEORY-1659](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1659.md) | Fanning and Raworth (2025) find that, measured as 35 indicators each against its own social or planetary threshold, global social shortfall fell modestly between 2000 and 2022 while ecological overshoot grew, and that disaggregating by income cluster shows the richest fifth of countries contributing over 40% of overshoot and the poorest 40% bearing over 60% of shortfall, an inequality the global aggregates mask. | Fanning & Raworth (2025), read in [NOTE-1782](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1782.md) (Read). Globally, deprivation fell modestly while ecological overshoot rose; disaggregated, the richest cluster contributes a disproportionate share of overshoot and the poorest holds most shortfall. | Proposed |
